items.title: A question of region
items.description: “Don’t know much about history, don’t know much biology, Don’t know much about the science book, don’t know much about the French I took…” THIS is an old song, which seems to be an apt description of journalists — especially in Pakistan. Over the decades, the profession has moved on from print to television and now digital but our training remains rooted in old-fashioned ‘generalism’ (if there’s such a word). As with the bureaucrats who run petroleum one day and health the other, we journalists move from commenting on foreign affairs one evening to the economy and healthcare the next. The notion of specialising in issues or studying them in depth is as alien to us as democracy is to Islamabad’s neighbours. Perhaps this is why most in the profession rarely bother with reading and books. Take history — even of Pakistan. Those of us who entered the field at the time of newspapers learnt the country’s history through oral tradition. Late-night chats with senior colleagues, who had survived martial laws and newsroom working hours, told us of tumultuous times such as war, secession and dictatorship. They included those who remembered what it was like working during the censorship of Ziaul Haq’s times, the night Pervez Musharraf removed the government or when an operation was first launched against the MQM in Karachi. The oral history we learnt alongside copy editing was the best counter-narrative to the whitewashed account taught in school books under Pakistan Studies. Our daastango provided us with a fun but patchy account of the land of the pure. Patchy, for it leaves us with more questions than answers — the personal accounts that we learn history from are rooted in Pakistan but are a little sketchy on details of the region. Few journalists have travelled around the region and reported on other countries. As a result, many may point out similarities between Pakistan and Egypt (aren’t they obvious?) but few will note what makes them different and why. For a hack such as myself, the biggest difference is perhaps Pakistan’s impatience with its rulers. Our last dictator spent eight years in power, struggling in the last two. And in Egypt, Anwar Sadat spent 11 years in power, Hosni Mubarak around three decades, while Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has been ruling for 12 and is still going strong. Closer to Pakistan, the Gulf states in general have also enjoyed stability and long reigns without much pressure from below. Evidently, this is due to oil, but can it explain everything? After all, Iran is no less oil-rich and yet it went through a revolution, which perhaps remains unprecedented as a political event in the region. Despite the authoritarianism of both the Shah and the theocracy that followed, Iran has demonstrated that its people believe in resistance. In recent years, they have pushed back multiple times against crackdowns; at times they have even compelled the state to change course. This is a strain missing in Iran’s neighbours to the west. Crowded, noisy and poor, societies in this region struggle with imperfect democracies. But to its east, it’s a different story. Pakistan and the rest of South Asia, in comparison to its western neighbours in the Middle East, are poorer and noisier. Is this why this region has avoided the kind of authoritarianism that marks the Middle East? Crowded, noisy and poor, societies in this region continue to struggle with flawed and imperfect democracies; there is flirtation with authoritarianism but on paper most of them adhere or aspire to the framework left by the British. This is true of Pakistan where martial law dictators have also worked hard to prove their democratic credentials by holding elections. And with it comes the inability of rulers in the region to lord it over their citizens for long periods. Indeed, in recent years, Hasina Wajed’s 15 years in power has been quite a feat. In India, Jawaharlal Nehru and Narendra Modi have also enjoyed prime ministerships for a similar period of time. On the other hand, in Pakistan, the longest power stints have been a bit shorter. In a tradition closer to Iran, South Asia has also pushed back against dictators of the civilian (Wajed) and military (Musharraf) type, with street protests forcing them to call it a day. Strongmen such as Modi have also been bested by students armed with their wit and social media, while in Pakistan, authoritarian establishments have struggled to clamp down on criticism on X. This is not entirely new: back in the 1970s, both Indira Gandhi’s imposition of the Emergency and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto’s authoritarian rule came to an end, albeit in very different ways. In one country, the democratic system pushed back while in the other, the military establishment did so. With all our problems, Pakistan’s journalists still sit in talk shows and complain about the censorship they face; their counterparts in nearby regions are perhaps not allowed to whine thus on live television. In most countries with censorship, journalists usually spend their time complaining about absolute freedom. There is an ‘argumentative’ South Asian that shapes this region differently from its western neighbours. And perhaps also its eastern ones. Travel east to Myanmar and here once again, regimes tend to become more authoritarian and more long-lasting. The long detention of Aung San Suu Kyi under a martial law regime illustrates this best. After a short experiment with elections and civilian control, Myanmar has returned to military rule but one in which contestation by the people has turned to civil war. While this may seem alien to Pakistanis, it is worrying that in parts of our country we, too, face a situation where the state appears to only control the cities. But what eventually determines the different state-society relationships in these countries? Why is Myanmar able to sustain military rule while Bangladesh is not? Or why has Pakistan, despite its close ties to the Middle East, not been able to impose a similar system of government? Now if I hadn’t learnt history in newsrooms and had read more, perhaps I could have answered some of these questions. The writer is a journalist. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: High-powered body to probe death of family in ‘locked flat’ in Karachi's Ahsanabad
items.description: KARACHI: While investigators said they have so far found no evidence to suggest that the death of five members of a family in an Ahsanabad apartment was a homicide, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Javed Alam Odho has decided to establish a high-powered body to investigate the incident that has sent shock waves through the city. The couple, identified as Dr Umer, 45, and Mehwish, 35, their daughter Zainab, 10, and two other minor daughters were found dead on Sunday inside a room of the flat located on the seventh floor of the building, officials said, adding that the bodies were recovered after the door, which was locked from the inside, was broken open. On Monday, IGP Odho asked the city police chief to form a committee and make highly trained investigating officers and forensic experts its part. “All facts of the incident should be brought to light with the help of modern investigative and technical means,” he said, adding: “No aspect should be overlooked during the investigation process and the probe should be taken to its logical conclusion on the basis of evidence.” City police chief says investigations underway but no evidence of homicide found so far Karachi police chief Azad Khan told Dawn that the exact cause of death had not yet been ascertained. “So far, no evidence had emerged to suggest that it was a homicide. It had been verified that the doctor was facing acute financial problems and had also been diagnosed with kidney cancer. He had left his job at a private hospital. However, no final conclusion could be drawn at this stage,” he said. As the corpses were shifted to the Edhi morgue, an Edhi Foundation spokesperson said that the bodies were handed over to their relatives late on Monday evening. The city police chief said that the deceased doctor’s brother and father-in-law had arrived in the city from Punjab in the evening. He said investigators would take the relatives to the spot and conduct a thorough search in their presence. He said that an FIR had not been registered yet. East SSP Investigation Mohammed Usman Sadozai told Dawn: “We are investigating the case from every possible angle.” SITE Superhighway Industrial Area SHO Mohammed Nawaz said that neighbours had informed the police that the doctor had been a victim of street crime. The neighbours also told the police about tough financial conditions the family was undergoing. The SHO said not a single penny was found in the flat, while the kitchen and refrigerator were also empty. He said after his diagnosis, the doctor had reportedly stopped going to the hospital where he worked since August without any intimation. The hospital administration told the police that they tried to persuade him not to quit as they would arrange for his treatment but he left the job. He formally resigned from the hospital on Sept 15, saying that he was going to Punjab for his treatment. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

Islamabad, Rawalpindi brace for protest as security preparations intensify
items.description: • Capital police seek Rs827m to handle marchers • Over 2,000 containers deployed at key points in Islamabad, Attock • Police expect 20,000 to 25,000 protesters • Schools, colleges being used for police accommodation closed ISLAMABAD: Residents of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad and their adjoining areas are set to brace for another possible confrontation between the personnel of the law enforcement agencies and protesters, as the police have already deployed more than 2,000 containers at various locations in the capital and at Attock Bridge, an entry point to the Punjab from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern parts of the country. The Islamabad police have requested Rs827 million to bear expenses related to the planned protests by the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI), Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and Kissan Ittehad . The amount will be spent on container rents, accommodation, food and transportation of police personnel and the purchase of anti-riot equipment, including tear-gas shells and rubber bullets. Background interviews with some of the police officials revealed that the authorities are expecting between 20,000 and 25,000 protesters to gather in Islamabad. According to them, the PTI’s long march is expected to begin from various parts of the country on Sept 27 and may reach the capital within three to four days. They have been directed that all security arrangements should be in place by Sept 26 evening. They further expect that the situation may continue for about a week or so. They told Dawn that arrangements had been made to “intercept” the protesters outside Islamabad. However, a final decision will be made under the guidance and orders of the government. Sources said various contractors had committed to providing 1,550 containers, including 350 required to seal the Red Zone. A wall of containers has already been erected around the Red Zone, with the police placing containers on roads as well as on greenbelts along its boundary. Out of these containers, around 1,000 will be used to block entry points, major roads and highways and the high security zone, from Margalla Road to Faisal Avenue, Khayaban-i-Suhrawardy and Third Avenue, besides the Expressway, Srinagar Highway and other major roads. The Red Zone has seven designated entry points, including Khayaban-i-Suhrawardy, the Old Parade Ground/Jinnah Avenue, and Aga Khan Road. Gates at these points will also be closed. After placing the containers at the entry points and on major roads, they are being welded together and filled with gravel and sand to prevent their removal. The police have requested 16,000 police personnel and 4,000 anti-riot kits from the Punjab Police and 2,000 officials and 3,000 anti-riot kits from Sindh Police. Besides, three deputy inspectors general of police, seven senior superintendents of police, and 18 superintendents of police have also been called from the Punjab and Sindh. Besides arranging containers, the contractors have also been asked to arrange 70 coasters, 30 double cabins and buses which will be used to transport the police force. About 50 portable washrooms and toilets were also being arranged for the police near the duty points. Educational institutions closed Over four dozen buildings have been acquired for lodging of the police personnel. The buildings include government schools, marquees and other government buildings, like Sports Complex and Pak-China Friendship Centre. The police personnel from the provinces are likely to start arriving in the capital from today (Tuesday). Educational institutions where accommodation has been arranged for the visiting police personnel are being closed from today (Tuesday) and the students and their parents have already been informed about the decision. Islamabad Deputy Commissioner Irfan Nawaz Memon was approached for comment but did not respond. The extensive deployment of containers and closure of major roads and entry points are likely to cause serious inconvenience to commuters in Islamabad and Rawalpindi. With key routes such as the Expressway, Srinagar Highway, Margalla Road and roads leading to the Red Zone expected to face restrictions, motorists may have to use alternative routes, leading to prolonged travelling times and traffic congestion. Commenting on the frequent protests in the capital, a diplomat once stated during an informal gathering that “Islamabad has five seasons – summer, winter, spring, autumn and containers.” Rawalpindi Additional security measures have been introduced in Rawalpindi’s “Red Zone”, including the establishment of nine police pickets. A special security plan has been chalked out by the police, under which personnel will be deployed at the pickets round the clock in two 12-hour shifts. According to sources, foolproof security arrangements have been made to protect important government buildings and installations located in the Red Zone, stretching from The Mall of Rawalpindi to the old airport. Special police pickets have been established at The Mall, MH Chowk, TM Flashman Chowk, Metro Station Saddar Chowk, T&T Chowk, RA Bazaar Road, Chungi No. 22, Shalimar Chowk and Marka-i-Haq Square. The Dolphin Force will also patrol designated areas round the clock. The concerned DSPs and SHOs have been tasked with checking hotels and inns as part of the security arrangements. Attock Security arrangements have been intensified across Attock district, a key entry point, with containers and sand-filled bags being placed at strategic crossings linking Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Punjab. A large number of containers have reportedly been positioned at Attock Bridge and Haroon Bridge, two major crossings connecting KP with Punjab. The security measures are particularly focused on GT Road and motorway routes near Haroon Bridge, where sandbags have reportedly been placed on both sides of the road. According to sources, security has also been tightened at other important entry and exit points, including Chach and Ghazi interchanges, while additional police personnel from different districts have been mobilised. Punjab Police sources said around 30,000 personnel, including senior officers, were being deployed in Attock as part of a wider security plan for the planned protest. Educational institutions in Hazro city have reportedly been closed temporarily. Some schools have also been earmarked to accommodate police personnel deployed for security duties. The Attock crossings are considered strategically important because they provide major road links between KP, northern Punjab and the Islamabad-Rawalpindi region, making Hazro and the surrounding bridges a key focal point of preparations for the proposed march. — Mohammad Asghar from Rawalpindi and Amjad Iqbal from Taxila also contributed to the report Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Civil service reform
items.description: PAKISTAN cannot become a modern state as long as its bureaucracy continues to be organised around hierarchy, seniority and generalist recruitment. The system has become better at managing careers than solving problems. It rewards position rather than expertise and performance, and protects procedure more readily than outcomes. Moreover, a bureaucracy built primarily for routine administration can hardly meet the ever-growing economic, technological, environmental and social challenges confronting the government. It is against this backdrop that a ‘new’ civil service restructuring plan has been unveiled by the planning minister. The plan proposes professional cadres, seeks changes to the CSS examination, opens up senior posts to wider competition and links performance to rewards. It also proposes a new civil-service training structure. These ideas may not be new but they do make sense. However, the problem is that the plan represents a piecemeal approach. Several reform programmes were proposed in the last couple of decades; none was implemented due to resistance from bureaucracy and lack of political will. This plan could have provided a useful starting point for comprehensive civil service reform had it not cherry-picked proposals from an earlier reform exercise. The report, on which the new proposals draw, was prepared by the Institutional Reforms Committee headed by Dr Ishrat Husain in 2021, and covered recruitment, training, career progression, specialisation, performance management, accountability and the structure of the senior bureaucracy. It explicitly said that civil service reform had to be holistic. Reforming one segment of the system without addressing the others, it warned, could backfire. That raises the more important question: why are these proposals being put forward again, instead of building on the earlier blueprint? The government needs to explain what happened to the previous reform exercise, which of its recommendations were implemented, which were rejected and why. Instead, the government appears to have taken selected recommendations from it. That risks producing another reorganisation plan without actually changing the way the bureaucracy and state function. Civil service reform is not about creating new cadres, changing examination rules or merging training institutions. It is about changing incentives and institutional behaviour. The state needs specialists who can understand increasingly complex problems. It needs managers who can deliver. It needs promotion based on performance rather than seniority alone. And it needs accountability that applies to failure as much as success. Most importantly, reform requires consistency. The 2021 blueprint already provided much of the framework needed for this. If it fell short of anything, it should have been fixed instead of being discarded. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: South African Women Need Protection, Not Warnings
items.description: Click to expand Image A student during a vigil for victims of gender-based violence and femicide at the University of Cape Town, South Africa, September 18, 2026. © 2026 Esa Alexander/Reuters The discovery of several women’s bodies on the outskirts of South Africa’s commercial capital, Johannesburg, has caused fear, anxiety and outrage across the country. All the women were found naked or partially clothed, according to police. Some of the bodies had bruising. At least three suspects are already in custody as authorities continue to examine possible links between the killings. These mysterious killings of women are not isolated crimes but part of a longstanding crisis about gender-based violence in South Africa. Earlier in 2026, Human Rights Watch noted that systemic criminal justice failures impede women in South Africa from accessing justice, while survivors have limited access to psychosocial support. Human Rights Watch has also documented that sex workers, LGBT people, and undocumented women face additional barriers to protection and redress. The South African Medical Research Council has in the past, estimated that nearly seven women were killed each day in the country, including three by an intimate partner. Police failed to identify a suspect in about 44 percent of cases. South Africa’s Constitution and other regional and international laws guarantee the rights to equality, dignity, life, and freedom and security of the person, including freedom from violence from public or private sources. Following the killings, South African police urged women to avoid walking or exercising alone. These types of warnings shift responsibility to the victim and cannot substitute for effective measures to prevent and respond to gender-based violence. The authorities instead should conduct safety audits in affected communities, improve lighting and police visibility, strengthen efforts to prevent and address domestic violence, and respond rapidly when women are reported missing. The authorities should have adequate resources to investigate and prosecute these cases, and keep families informed as they do. President Cyril Ramaphosa, who has condemned the killings, said that South Africa must stand up for women’s “rights, safety and dignity.” That requires more than condolences and warnings. It requires effective and immediate government action that enables women to live, work, travel, and participate in public life freely and safely.

items.title: Pakistan, Saudi sign agreement to abolish visa requirements for official, diplomatic passports holders
items.description: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed an agreement on Tuesday to abolish visa requirements for holders of diplomatic, official and special passports. Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar signed the agreement with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal Bin Farhan on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, he said in a post on X. DPM Dar hoped the step would “further facilitate high-level engagement and institutional exchanges, and contribute to advancing our enduring and brotherly strategic partnership across all areas of mutual interest”. The two countries share robust bilateral cooperation, with frequent high-level diplomatic exchanges on both sides. On August 7, ​​​​​​​Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, alongside Turkiye, also signed a joint defence agreement pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond. Later that month, the two countries agreed to boost Pakistani agricultural and food exports to the Gulf state up to $3 billion. The agreement was reached during the visit of a Saudi delegation led by Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture Engineer Abdulrahman Al-Fadley. In July, Saudi Arabia had also launched a multiple-entry Umrah visa with one-year validity from the date of issuance, enabling pilgrims to enter the kingdom multiple times, with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days each year. In 2024, in another relief, Riyadh eased tourist visa requirements for Pakistani travellers, allowing them to submit a bank statement showing a minimum monthly credit amount of $750 or its equivalent.

items.title: Trump lleva sus batallas a la Asamblea General de Naciones Unidas
items.description: Donald Trump llega a Nueva York con ganas de batalla. Este martes hablará ante la Asamblea General de la ONU en un momento en el que se le acumulan los problemas en casa, donde la inflación no da respiro y las encuestas anticipan malas noticias para los republicanos en las elecciones de medio mandato, y en Oriente Próximo, donde los hutíes de Yemen amenazan con extender aún más la guerra por la región. La aventura bélica en la que se metió en Irán, de la que ahora no sabe cómo salir , será uno de los focos de atención en Naciones Unidas esta semana. “El presidente destacará cómo él y su Administración han afrontado problemas complejos en todo el mundo. […] Abordará la importancia de garantizar que Irán nunca posea un arma nuclear”, según explicó el viernes el embajador de Estados Unidos ante la ONU, Mike Waltz. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El ‘caso Begoña Gómez’ entra en la era pos-Peinado: ¿qué plazos se manejan para el juicio?, ¿testificará Pedro Sánchez?
items.description: El magistrado Juan Carlos Peinado ha dirigido durante dos años y cinco meses una investigación cargada de polémica contra Begoña Gómez, esposa del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez. Por primera vez en la historia democrática de España, un juez instructor ha imputado, ha procesado y ha enviado al banquillo ( decisión que firmó este mismo lunes , apenas seis días antes de jubilarse) a la pareja de un jefe del Ejecutivo. Aunque la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid ha encauzado parte de sus pesquisas y ha marcado la senda por donde el sumario podía prosperar, Peinado ha encabezado la iniciativa para que se siente a Gómez ante un jurado popular formado por nueve ciudadanos. Pero, a partir de ahora, queda ya todo lejos de las manos del cuestionado magistrado. Comienza, en palabras de fuentes cercanas al caso, la “era pos-Peinado”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sánchez se enteró en el avión a Nueva York del juicio a Begoña Gómez: los grandes hitos del caso coinciden con viajes del presidente
items.description: Una vez más, una decisión muy relevante del juez Peinado sobre el caso Begoña Gómez llega con el presidente, Pedro Sánchez, iniciando un viaje importante, esta vez a la cumbre de la ONU en Nueva York. Ya es casi una constante sobre la que se bromea en La Moncloa. Esta vez, Sánchez no viaja a Nueva York con su esposa, pero en otras ocasiones sí estaba con ella en esos viajes marcados por las decisiones de Peinado y el impacto fue aún más fuerte. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las ONG, en el foco de la ira en Ceuta: “Nos acusan de provocar un efecto llamada”
items.description: Leticia, Diana e Irene venían en el ferri de Algeciras a Ceuta el domingo, hablando entre ellas. Habían dejado en Sevilla una furgoneta con material de primera necesidad, alimentos no perecederos, mantas y medicamentos reunidos por la asociación vecinal asturiana Esto ye Ciares para distribuir entre los migrantes de Ceuta sin plaza en los centros de acogida. La mujer en el asiento delantero se giró y les preguntó: “¿Venís a la manifestación?”. Ellas no estaban al tanto de la protesta que se produciría horas después bajo el lema “ SOS Ceuta invadida ”, así que le dijeron que no. “¿Entonces vais al campamento?, ¿sois las de la ONG esa?”, inquirió de nuevo la señora, visiblemente más iracunda. Ni Leticia ni Diana ni Irene estaban al tanto de que se refería la asociación pamplonesa Negu Gorriak/Derecho a Techo, que llegarían a Ceuta horas después y cuya trayectoria en barco había empezado a monitorear ya el grupo de WhatsApp de la Federación Provincial de Vecinos de Ceuta. Planeaban recibirles en la salida de vehículos del Puerto, localizaron la matrícula del furgón en el que llegarían y difundieron una convocatoria para salir a su encuentro con el lema “no queremos que los grupos radicales proetarras entren en Ceuta”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Francesca Thyssen, coleccionista: “La futura sede del museo no va a tener mi nombre, ya he superado esa etapa de vincular mi identidad al trabajo”
items.description: En el rostro de Francesca Thyssen-Bornemisza (Lausana, 68 años) se percibe satisfacción y cierto alivio. Han pasado dos días desde que el Museo Thyssen de Madrid anunciara que tendrá una segunda sede en el Palacio de Hielo , en 2032, a pocas calles de donde se encuentra el museo en el centro de Madrid, y donde se albergarán las 365 obras que la coleccionista ha donado y prestado a la institución. “Una para cada día del año”, dice, con una sonrisa, la fundadora de la colección TBA21 (sustentada en arte del siglo XXI) e hija del barón. Hace más de cuatro años que había anunciado su intención de que su legado acabara en el museo madrileño donde se reúne el de su padre y el de Carmen Cervera. Objetivo cumplido: más de 8.000 metros cuadrados para exponer sus obras y organizar otro tipo de actividades, todo financiado por el Estado. Seguir leyendo

items.title: De Tinder a las ‘Apps’ para correr: los móviles se convierten en un frente para reclutar, espiar y sabotear al enemigo
items.description: Las alarmas que han disparado la relación de un comandante español de la OTAN y una mujer de origen ruso que conoció por Tinder, la aplicación de citas , son el último capítulo en un nuevo campo de batalla del espionaje: las aplicaciones web. Compartir contenido en las redes sociales, publicar tu carrera matutina o buscar el amor en línea se han convertido en un riesgo latente para los ejércitos en todo el mundo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Vida y peligros de un detective hoy: “No quiero más sectas, me metí en una y casi me enganchan”
items.description: A Gómez, hombre casado de 39 años, unos conocidos le sorprendieron paseando con otra mujer a las tres de la madrugada en las ferias de Talavera. “Es una cosa muy dura. La presenté como mi amiga, pero notaba cómo estaban teniendo cortocircuitos en el cerebro. Sales de cervezas a las tantas con una señora que no es la tuya y, claro, la gente se bloquea”, lamenta. “Lo que ellos no saben es que yo no cometo infidelidades. ¡Las investigo!”. Al frente del despacho Wolf and Wolf Detectives, Gómez ejerce como investigador privado desde el municipio de la provincia de Toledo y, a menudo, se asocia con una colega, Herminia, de 40 años, que tiene también su propia agencia, Herminia AC, Detective & Criminóloga. En aquella ocasión, no perseguían una infidelidad, sino a una persona que estaba trabajando en la feria mientras se encontraba de baja en otra empresa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un arquitecto reinventa el piso oscuro y compartimentado de su vecino en el centro de Madrid
items.description: “Los primeros peldaños son siempre los más difíciles”. El arquitecto Gonzalo Pardo cita las Instrucciones para subir una escalera , de Julio Cortázar , para explicar su intervención en esta vivienda madrileña. Tiene dos razones. La escalera era lo más molesto del piso oscuro que se encontró. Hoy es la protagonista de su reforma: la que amplía visualmente la planta baja del dúplex, al no estar cerrada, la que actúa como pozo de luz —al tener doble altura—, la que convierte en almacén y banco su base y la que sirve para acceder a la estantería que recorre la pared. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Por qué todas las cremalleras llevan las letras YKK grabadas?
items.description: Mira la cremallera de tu chaqueta. Es muy posible que lleve tres letras: YKK. Mira la de tus pantalones. Y la de la mochila. No es casualidad: detrás de un detalle tan pequeño en un objeto tan aparentemente insignificante está uno de los gigantes industriales más curiosos del mundo. Según The Wall Street Journal , la marca japonesa vendió más de 10.000 millones de cremalleras en un solo año (son los últimos datos publicados, correspondientes a 2024). Son tantas que, colocadas en fila, superarían los tres millones de kilómetros: unas 80 vueltas a la Tierra. Y lo más llamativo es que no se trata de un récord aislado: YKK ya había superado los 10.000 millones en 2018 y 2021. Ante el otoño en el que los jerséis half-zip (con cremallera hasta el pecho) serán la tendencia de moda incontestable, ponemos el foco en esta empresa que lleva casi un siglo perfeccionando el mismo objeto. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Nación y razón
items.description: En las últimas semanas ha surgido, como una seta alucinógena, la propuesta de quitar la nacionalidad a los que se porten mal. Este delirio suele ser invocado por aquellos que se envuelven en la bandera para disimular otras carencias. La primera de las políticas discriminatorias del nazismo tuvo que ver con la persecución de todas aquellas expresiones, ya fueran artísticas o intelectuales, que identificaban como antialemanas. Esto generó una tradición germana y austriaca, tras la tragedia de la guerra, por la cual el desprecio a su propio país era casi una obligación estilística. El mejor representante de esta escuela fue Thomas Bernhard y sus compatriotas tuvieron que soportar su éxito y su categoría internacional para no identificarse como nazis encubiertos bajo el sistema democrático. Pero los tiempos están en regresión y vuelve a invocarse lo antipatriótico, como si no hubiera formas de ser de un país a gusto de cada cual. El precedente más cercano ha sido la dictadura de Nicaragua, donde la pareja en el poder expulsó y convirtió en apátridas a los más nobles representantes del pensamiento crítico . Algunos de ellos han encontrado refugio en España, algo que honra a nuestro país. También El Salvador encarcela sin garantías a los nacionales y Donald Trump, un presidente dañino, juega con la idea de cerrar universidades, expulsar alumnos, vetar medios e impedir el voto electoral si no piensan como él. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El DIN A4 de Mourinho
items.description: El veinteañero irrumpe en la habitación sin pensarlo. No importa que sean las nueve de la noche o, lo que es lo mismo, plena madrugada para cualquier madre de familia. Necesita enseñar algo de manera urgente. “Mira, mira”, repite, casi aplastando el móvil en la cara de su interlocutora. El objeto de tanta excitación es el papel impreso DIN A4, a todo color, con dos jugadas de fútbol que blande José Mourinho en una rueda de prensa después de que el Real Madrid pierda el derbi contra el Atlético. “Es increíble”, repite el chaval, regodeándose con los vídeos de TikTok que se mofan del entrenador, que se defiende a la antigua, con papel y boli. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La Izquierda rompe la alternancia en Berlín y acaricia la alcaldía con la promesa de abaratar la vivienda
items.description: Desde la reunificación alemana, los conservadores y socialdemócratas se han alternado siempre en el poder como los partidos más votados en Berlín. Hasta el pasado domingo . El partido de Die Linke (La Izquierda) ha dejado de estar limitado tradicionalmente a los barrios del este para alzarse como el partido más votado de Berlín impulsado por una campaña centrada, principalmente, en la lucha contra la escasez y los precios de la vivienda. La germano-turca Elif Eralp puede convertirse así en la primera alcaldesa de Berlín de la formación izquierdista, aunque para lograrlo necesitará un acuerdo de coalición con ecologistas y socialdemócratas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Recta final para el regreso de Puigdemont: el Constitucional decidirá desde el 6 de octubre sobre el último obstáculo del Supremo a la amnistía
items.description: La que quizá sea la gran paradoja de la ley de junio de 2024 de amnistía al procés —que no se haya aplicado todavía al líder del proceso independentista que se pretendía superar— enfila el camino de su resolución. A partir del primer pleno de octubre, el día 6, el Tribunal Constitucional tomará ya una decisión definitiva sobre los recursos de amparo presentados por aquellos políticos independentistas catalanes a los que el Supremo decidió no aplicar la amnistía por el delito de malversación —el expresidente de la Generalitat, Carles Puigdemont, y otros dos huidos de la justicia española; así como del vicepresidente, Oriol Junqueras, y otros tres dirigentes condenados por malversación tras el juicio del Tribunal Supremo de 2019—. El ponente del primer proyecto de sentencia del Constitucional sobre dichos recursos, el magistrado conservador José María Macías, hará suya hoy mismo esa interpretación del Supremo, que será rechazada por la mayoría progresista. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Trabajo propone un programa público para que 200.000 jóvenes accedan a su primer empleo hasta 2028
items.description: El Ministerio de Trabajo ha abierto este lunes una nueva mesa de diálogo social con los sindicatos y la patronal para rediseñar las políticas activas de empleo destinadas a los colectivos de jóvenes y parados de larga duración de más edad (de entre 45 y más de 55 años, según la medida) a partir del año que viene. Estas políticas incluyen formación, incentivos a la contratación o mejoras en los procesos de búsqueda de empleo e intermediación laboral. Entre las principales novedades para los más jóvenes, Trabajo propone un Programa de primera experiencia profesional , con acciones específicas de los servicios públicos de empleo e itinerarios personalizados específicos que se coloca como meta que al menos 200.000 jóvenes hayan accedido a su primer empleo para 2028. Estos puestos podrán ubicarse tanto en el sector privado como en el público. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Pedro Corbalán, el hombre que visitó el ático, negoció la compra, firmó la confidencialidad y que Ayuso no quiere que hable
items.description: Pedro Corbalán Ruiz es el CEO de la empresa pública que compró el ático de lujo en Chamberí y también fue quien gestionó la operación, que tan solo conocía un puñado de personas. El consejero delegado de Planifica Madrid contactó con la inmobiliaria de La Moraleja ―aunque no se sabe quién dio la orden―, visitó el inmueble, firmó el contrato de arras de 630.000 euros y también el acuerdo de confidencialidad que blindaba la adquisición, según han confirmado a EL PAÍS fuentes conocedoras de los detalles de la compraventa, y consta en varios documentos que la Comunidad de Madrid publicó el jueves para explicar la opaca compra. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Plan Alquila Madrid: la web “prehistórica” de la Comunidad para encontrar casa de alquiler que cuesta 750.000 euros anuales
items.description: Si usted busca un piso para alquilar en la Comunidad de Madrid, hay un enlace con el logo oficial del Gobierno madrileño que le invita a entrar en la web del Plan Alquila. Si se hace clic, se avanzará hasta una página web fundada en el año 2008. Una página web de letras diminutas, casi ilegibles. Puede que la inteligencia artificial avance a un ritmo vertiginoso, pero la web del Plan Alquila —por la que la Comunidad paga 750.000 euros al año a la empresa Factoría Digital por la gestión e ideada para facilitar el alquiler de los madrileños— lleva otros ritmos, está detenida en el tiempo desde hace casi dos décadas. Eso sí, el Plan Alquila tiene un mapa gigantesco con toda la región que promete mostrarle todas las ofertas disponibles. Un mapa que está roto. Un mapa que no funciona. Un mapa vacío: según el mapa, no hay ninguna vivienda en alquiler en la región madrileña. Un mapa de viviendas de alquiler en la Comunidad de Madrid donde no hay ni una sola vivienda de alquiler en la Comunidad de Madrid. Solo si se fija usted en una pequeña pestaña con el nombre de “Listado” podrá ver que en estos momentos Plan Alquila tiene “anunciadas” 140 casas en la capital y otras tantas en diversos municipios. Por desgracia, esto tampoco es así. Un porcentaje significativo son inmuebles que ya están alquilados, aunque aquí aparezcan como disponibles. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Gobierno y la Junta retrasan la declaración como sobreexplotados de los acuíferos andaluces, pese a que muchos se secan
items.description: El nivel de muchos acuíferos andaluces está en caída libre pese al respiro temporal que supusieron las copiosas lluvias del año pasado. Cada vez más comarcas del interior sufren para mantener el abastecimiento de su población ante la merma de sus masas subterráneas. Para sobrevivir a esta alarmante escasez, el primer paso es declarar el acuífero “en riesgo”, denominación actual de sobreexplotado, para así primar las extracciones esenciales para el consumo humano, condicionar las recreativas y atajar de una vez los pozos ilegales. Es decir, poner orden para saber cómo se ha esquilmado el subsuelo hídrico. De momento, en la región hay seis acuíferos declarados sobreexplotados, según cifras oficiales. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El milagro de ‘Romeo + Julieta’: cómo Leo DiCaprio, Claire Danes y Baz Luhrmann reinventaron a Shakespeare
items.description: Hace treinta años, un jovencísimo Leonardo DiCaprio de solo 21 años asaltó el corazón de media humanidad al protagonizar junto a Claire Danes, Romeo + Julieta , una adaptación de la obra clásica de William Shakespeare dirigida y adaptada por Baz Luhrmann. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Darth Vader convive con Picasso y Banksy: el ambicioso museo de George Lucas desembarca en Los Ángeles
items.description: Contar el mundo a través de imágenes. La humanidad lo lleva haciendo desde hace milenios: desde las pinturas primitivas hasta la la fotografía, el cine, la televisión del salón, las pantallas omnipresentes hoy. Si a lo largo de las últimas décadas alguien ha sabido crear emociones a través de las imágenes, ese es George Lucas, de 82 años, director, escritor, productor y mente pensante detrás de fenómenos que han moldeado la cultura contemporánea, como Star Wars e Indiana Jones . Su buen ojo no solo ha estado en el cine sino también, durante décadas (gracias a los jugosos beneficios del cine), desde que era universitario, en el arte, con una inmensa colección de unas 40.000 obras que, ahora, ha decidido compartir con el mundo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Salvar a la ONU
items.description: La Asamblea General de la ONU, que arranca hoy en Nueva York , será un termómetro de las extraordinarias tensiones globales que vivimos y también del estado de la propia institución, que ha sufrido en los últimos años una persistente tarea de demolición hasta el punto de asomarse a la irrelevancia. Los jefes de Estado y de Gobierno se reúnen esta semana en un foro que, en tiempos normales, debería situarse en el centro de las discusiones sobre las guerras y el hambre, sobre un cambio climático que se abate con virulencia sobre nuestras sociedades, y sobre la aceleración desbocada de la inteligencia artificial. Pero estos no son tiempos normales. Y la ONU se encuentra hoy maniatada, con un Consejo de Seguridad inoperante y sin credibilidad y al mismo tiempo sometida a brutales recortes de fondos y a un desprecio hacia sus valores fundacionales que parte precisamente de Estados Unidos, el mismo país que contribuyó a la construcción de este orden internacional hoy en ruinas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Polarización e impotencia
items.description: La profundidad de la grieta que divide a las sociedades actuales es motivo de preocupación en todas partes. La gente se agrupa por bloques ideológicos. La pertenencia a uno de estos bloques moldea valores, estilos de vida y visiones del mundo. En el enfrentamiento entre bloques, se exageran tanto las diferencias que parece desvanecerse cualquier posibilidad de entendimiento mutuo . Donde antes había un terreno común, ahora se abre una brecha infranqueable. Quienes pertenecen a un bloque no pueden entender que haya gente que pertenezca al contrario. A quien milita en el bloque opuesto se le da por perdido, se le ve como alguien irrecuperable, presa de una ceguera ideológica que le impide reconocer la realidad. Woody Allen, que siempre ha tenido mucho ojo sociológico, lo reflejó de forma muy divertida en Todos dicen I Love You (1996): a unos padres adinerados que vivían en una casa maravillosa en Nueva York, ambos demócratas puros, uno de los hijos les salía republicano convencido y lo llevaban al neurólogo para averiguar qué andaba mal en su cerebro. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Vaticano opta por no esconder el encuentro del Papa con víctimas de pederastia en Francia, tras el polémico secretismo en su viaje a España
items.description: El Papa viaja este viernes a Francia para una visita de cuatro días y en el programa detallado comunicado a la prensa este lunes aparece algo que no estaba en el que hizo a España en junio : se informa de que reunirá con víctimas de pederastia a las seis de la tarde del próximo domingo en el santuario de Lourdes. Es un cambio notable respecto a lo ocurrido en su visita a España el pasado mes de junio, donde la cita se excluyó del programa, primó el secretismo y nadie quería confirmar siquiera que se fuera a producir. Hasta el punto de que el Vaticano, de forma anómala, tuvo que hacer un comunicado horas antes del viaje para aclarar que sí habría un encuentro y lanzar un dardo: “El encuentro ha sido organizado por la Iglesia española”. Así que esta vez ha optado por no esconder nada y decirlo abiertamente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El ‘no’ a La Palma anticipa el final del Telescopio de Treinta Metros: “El proyecto está muerto”
items.description: El no a España puede ser el final del Telescopio de Treinta Metros (TMT), un megaproyecto en el que ya se han gastado 1.000 millones de dólares, opinan varias fuentes de la candidatura oficial para traer el ingenio a la isla de La Palma. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Conducir patinetes eléctricos multiplica el riesgo de lesiones graves por encima de ir en bici o en moto
items.description: Los usuarios de patinetes eléctricos tienen más riesgo de sufrir lesiones cerebrales y en órganos internos que los motociclistas y ciclistas. Es lo que asegura un estudio publicado este verano. El estudio analizó los datos de más de 15.000 pacientes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Chinese visitors to Gilgit-Baltistan may get visa on arrival
items.description: • Proposal for entry to Hunza, Nagar discussed at SIFC •One-window NOC portal to streamline clearance at Sost • Final rollout pending clearance from higher authorities GILGIT: Pakistan is considering special visa-on-arrival arrangements for Chinese tourists travelling to Gilgit-Baltistan through the Khunjerab Pass, with officials proposing a pilot programme initially covering Hunza and Nagar districts to promote cross-border tourism and economic activity. The proposal was discussed during a high-level meeting titled “Restora­t­i­­on of Visa Facility on Arri­val at Sost for Chinese Tou­rists” held at the Special In­­­vestment Facilitation Council (SIFC) Secretariat at the Prime Minister’s Office in Islamabad on Sept 15. The session, chaired by the joint secretary for SW-B at the SIFC, brought together officials from the Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) home and tourism departments, the Pakistan Tourism De­­v­elopment Corporation, the ministries of inter-provincial coordination, interior and foreign affairs, Pakis­t­­an Association of Tour Ope­­rators (Pato) and Green Tourism Pakistan Limited. According to the meeting minutes, the foreign affairs ministry expressed no objection in principle to the proposal, subject to security clearance. The interior ministry, however, noted that visa-on-arrival access had been suspended for all countr­i­­es after security concerns prompted a policy change at the highest level, and said any exception for Chi­nese nationals would need approval at the same level. Delegates from the Fed­e­­­ration of Pakistan Cham­bers of Commerce and Ind­ustry (FPCCI) argued that expanding Chinese tourism could boost foreign ex­­c­­hange earnings, create jobs and stimulate local economies, at a time when Pakistan is seeking greater foreign investment. Officials and stakeholders from GB proposed that a special or trial arrangement for Chinese tourists could be considered. They said tourism underpinned livelihoods across the region and that a downturn in visitor numbers, driven by wider global instability, had hit local businesses hard. Officials pointed to Hunza-Nagar’s existing tourism infrastructure and said no significant security threat had been identified along the proposed route. The GB government expressed willingness to provide security arrangements for tourists. Raja Nazimul Amin, adviser to the president on international trade and tourism investment at FPCCI, who attended the meeting, told Dawn that all relevant stakeholders had agreed to special arrangements for on-arrival visas for Chinese tourists travelling through the Khunj­erab Pass in phases. “Initially, it has been proposed that the visa on arrival will be given to Chinese tourists up to Hunza and Nagar districts under phase one,” Amin said. “If the trial basis remains successful, then it would be extended to the whole of Gilgit-Baltistan in phase two.” Mr Amin said the plan could generate billions of dollars in economic activity. He said the recommendations would be forwar­d­­ed to Prime Minister She­hbaz Sharif for appro­val, which he expected to be granted. Meanwhile, the Minis­try of Inter-Provincial Coordi­nation (MOIPC) called for the visa process to be stre­amlined, proposing a single online portal for no-objection certificates (NOCs). The GB Home Depart­m­ent, which currently issues NOCs through a multi-step police clearance process, agreed to explore a more efficient one-window system at Sost. The SIFC has asked the GB government to submit a detailed proposal. The plan will then go to MOIPC, before being referred to the interior and foreign ministries for concurrence and passed to higher authorities for a final decision. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: 4 terrorists die in Panjgur intelligence-based operation: officials
items.description: QUETTA: Security forces killed four more terrorists belonging to a banned organisation in an intelligence-based operation carried out in two areas of Panjgur district, officials said on Monday. According to officials, security forces launched an IBO on the information about the presence of armed militants in Koh-Prom and the Aphan area of Panjgur district. “Four armed terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan were killed in the heavy gunbattle during the operation,” they said, adding that a large quantity of arms and ammunition was seized from the hideouts of the terrorists. During the last one week, security forces have killed more than 35 terrorists in multiple actions conducted in several parts of Balochistan under the Radd-ul-Fitna operation. Search for kidnapped Kharan DC continues; two cricketers abducted from Dera Bugti Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti praised the security personnel for the successful operation against militants in Panjgur. He said that these operations would continue until the complete elimination of terrorism and that the government was pursuing a policy of zero tolerance against elements hostile to the country. Search operation underway Meanwhile, investigators have found no clue to the whereabouts of the Kharan deputy commissioner, who was kidnapped alongside three others two days ago. DC Munir Soomro and three other people were kidnapped as they were travelling in a car the other day. Officials said that police and other security personnel were searching different areas to recover Mr Soomro, but had made no headway so far. They said that Mr Soomro was heading to Kharan from Quetta along with his driver, a guard and another person in a private car. The armed men intercepted his car in Lajah area of Kharan district and took it along with their car. Police said that after receiving information about the missing deputy commissioner, several attempts were made to establish a contact with him through his cellphone, but his phone was found silent. The provincial administration has involved tribal elders of the area to contact the kidnappers for their safe release, but no progress has been made. Meanwhile, two local cricketers were kidnapped near the Kachhi Canal area in Dera Bugti. According to police, Zakir and Wadan Bugti, residents of Sui, were returning home after playing a match in Kandhkot when they were stopped by armed men near the Kachhi Canal area. After their abduction, security personnel cordoned off the area and launched a search operation. No one has claimed responsibility for the kidnapping of the two cricketers so far. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Govt tactics pushing people towards revolt: Fazl
items.description: ISLAMABAD: With the country facing mounting debt pressure and inflation, the government’s attempt to lock down the federal capital to counter protests will only encourage rebellious tendencies among the people, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman said. Speaking at a news conference at his residence on Monday after a central council meeting of his party, the JUI-F chief demanded that parliament should be taken into confidence on important national and foreign policy issues noting that the country was passing through a critical juncture. The JUI-F chief also called for an in-camera session of parliament on the regional security situation. The Maulana said some political parties had announced protests, but the government had filled Islamabad with containers ahead of the demonstrations. “By adopting such tactics, you are creating rebels yourself,” he said. JUI-F chief demands in-camera session of parliament on govt policies, regional security situation He said the PTI decided to hold protests and it was its right to do so. He recalled that the JUI-F had staged long marches in the past without causing damage to public property, saying even the Metro Bus service had continued to ply during the Lahore March. ‘Mediation role’ When asked by journalists, the JUI-F chief turned down the mediation offer and said that his party had reservations about this government. “We are an opposition party. How can we mediate?” he asked. He said dialogue could take place when there is a representative of the government. “The government should talk to those who are protesting. We ourselves are a party to the political dispute,” he said. The JUI-F chief said his party considered the hybrid government nothing but a representative of the military establishment and stressed that political dialogue required a government with genuine political authority. “We have decided to raise these issues from our own platform because economy and inflation are issues concerning everyone,” he said. The Maulana condemned the arrest of PTI founder’s sisters, saying political workers and parties should be allowed to exercise their constitutional right to hold protest rallies. He also criticised the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, questioning circumstances in which a provincial minister was allegedly shot and taken away. Referring to reports about possible constitutional amendments, the JUI-F chief said he would welcome provincial autonomy, but added that the issue should be discussed in the context of the constitutional position that existed 25 years ago. He said the party had played a key role in difficult circumstances in the past, recalling that in 2003 it spent 10 days working to help bring Pakistan-India relations out of a quagmire. He said the role played at that time should also be kept in view while discussing the political and diplomatic options available at the present. He alleged that the country had lost the confidence of Beijing. According to him, state institutions are in a defensive position while the country is facing serious internal challenges. “The country is in difficulty and we are sitting on a powder keg,” he said, adding that the issues confronting the country should be brought before the parliament. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

US has secretly deported 25,000 migrants, says report
items.description: NAIROBI: The United States has deported more than 25,000 people under secretive agreements with 35 countries to take migrants with no ties to those nations, according to an investigation published on Monday. Since US President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, Washington has been signing deals with developing countries to take migrants who cannot legally be sent home. The investigation by Forbidden Stories found the administration has earmarked $410 million to be paid directly to the receiving countries, or to UN agencies to facilitate the returns. At least 25,447 people had already been deported to third countries by August 31, 2026, according to data compiled by Forbidden Stories with a consortium of international journalists. The vast majority — around 20,000 — were sent to Mexico, but the rest were dispersed to 27 other countries across Latin America, Africa, and the Pacific, and agreements have been finalised with seven more. The deals vary, including over which nationalities can be deported and whether people with criminal records can be accepted. An investigation earlier this year found Washington is using visa bans and restrictions on African countries to strongarm them into accepting deportees. Lawyers said that deportees were being thrown into a “legal black hole”, held without charge in countries where they have no ties and few if any rights. Forbidden Stories said 49 of Africa’s 54 countries had been approached about accepting third-country deportees. A little-known State Department division called the Office of Remigration, created in May 2025, has handled most of the negotiations and payments, according to Forbidden Stories. The office is headed by Christian Jove Ehrhardt, a 41-year-old diplomat who previously worked as a security officer. The report details his visits to Cameroon, which signed a memorandum of understanding with the US in December on accepting deportees. A week later, it also signed a five-year health assistance programme worth nearly $400 million. The following month, the State Department said it would provide a further $30 million to the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) in Cameroon to “facilitate the voluntary return of refugees and combat illegal immigration.” The first plane carrying deportees arrived in Cameroon on January 14. Payments Other agreements have involved direct payments to governments. Palau, a small Pacific island nation with a population of under 18,000, signed an agreement in December 2025 to accept up to 75 third-country nationals in return for $7.5 million. However, only three people have so far been sent under the agreement. In Eswatini, 32 people have arrived since July 2025 out of a possible 160 under an agreement worth more than $5 million. It has accepted deportees with criminal records, the investigation found. Of the $410 million planned for the agreements, internal State Department records showed that $81 million was earmarked for signatory governments. The rest was intended for aid organisations, including more than $178 million for the UN’s International Organisation for Migration, and $123 million for UNHCR. The agencies have faced criticism over their involvement, although UNHCR told Forbidden Stories that it was not party to the bilateral agreements and that US funding was being used in line with its mandate to strengthen asylum systems. An IOM spokesperson told Forbidden Stories that the agency’s decisions to accept funding rested “on a single question: whether our engagement will improve the lives of the migrants affected. In these instances, we believe strongly it does.” Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Houthis push for control of Yemen’s highlands
items.description: • Trump speaks with Yemen’s president, doesn’t pledge military support • NYT says US president reversed decision on air strikes on Houthis DUBAI: Houthi fighters were pushing to seize strategic heights in Yemen on Monday to cut off the Red Sea coast from remaining areas held by Saudi-backed forces, after a report that President Donald Trump had called off US strikes on the group at the last minute. US President Trump spoke by phone with Yem­eni President Rashad al-Alimi on Sun­day, four people familiar with the matter said, discussing the advances of the Houthis around a vital global waterway. Alimi requested US support for his Saudi-backed government in its fight against the Houthis, who this month took key areas along the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive. Two of the sources, one Yemeni and one Western, said Trump had made no direct pledge of military support during the call. The White House and Yemen’s information minister did not immediately respond to requests for comment. On the other hand, a lightning advance by the Houthis this month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre. Strategic heights Five Yemeni military sources told Reu­ters that the Houthis were now seeking to seize strategic heights, known as the Kah­b­oub Mountains, in two provinces, Taiz and Lahij, which separate the Red Sea coast from the government-held south. Fighting has centred on the outskirts of the remote mountain Al-Wazi’iyah district in Taiz province, and Ras al-Ara along the Indian Ocean coast between the mouth of the Red Sea that the fighters captured last week and the government’s base in Aden. The Houthis aim to secure the rear of their forces around the Bab al-Mandab Strait leading into the Red Sea by taking control of the heights, which would allow them to open new fronts, according to the sources. That would help protect exposed positions the Houthis captured during their advance around Dhubab on the Red Sea and on Perim Island in the strait. The Houthis, who have controlled Yemen’s capital since 2014, seized the country’s Red Sea coast this month in a lightning advance that routed forces of an internationally recognised Yemeni government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia and based in the south. Saudi plea The New York Times reported that President Trump has changed his strategy on Yemen several times, torn betw­een Saudi pressure to strike the Iran-backed Houthis and the risk of opening another front in the Middle East war. It said Saudi Crown Prince Moham­med bin Salman called Trump on Sun­day “to implore him, again, to step in to help blunt the rapidly advancing group”. Trump had told his advisers the day before that he opposed strikes but chan­ged his mind after the call and “told the Pentagon to prepare for air strikes agai­nst the Houthis”, the newspaper repor­t­ed, citing anonymous administration officials. However, he appeared to have reve­rsed his decision again by midday Sunday, it said. Trump’s decision to pull back from striking the Houthis came as “commanders had approved target lists, troops were loading bombs onto US warplanes selected for the missions and the wave of attacks was just about to begin”, the Times said, citing two people briefed on the operation. US news platform Axios said Trump had already refused a Saudi request to strike the Houthis last week. Fox News reported on Sunday that Trump had said the Houthis have agreed not to hit US targets. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Italie : Meloni veut interdire le niqab et la burqa à l’école et limiter le nombre d’élèves étrangers
items.description: La Première ministre italienne Giorgia Meloni a annoncé la préparation d’un projet de loi visant à interdire le port de la burqa et du niqab dans les écoles et à instaurer un plafond légal pour le nombre d’élèves étrangers par classe. Le texte prévoit également des mesures liées à l’apprentissage de l’italien. Giorgia Meloni a annoncé dimanche 20 septembre la présentation prochaine, en Conseil des ministres, d’un ensemble de mesures consacrées à l’école. Parmi elles figurent l’interdiction du niqab et de la burqa dans les établissements scolaires, ainsi qu’une limitation du nombre d’élèves étrangers pouvant être accueillis dans une même classe. La cheffe du gouvernement a également indiqué que les parents d’élèves étrangers confrontés à de « graves difficultés d’intégration » dans le système scolaire pourraient être soumis à une obligation d’apprentissage de l’italien. Le plafond précis d’élèves étrangers par classe n’a toutefois pas encore été annoncé. Meloni a fait cette annonce lors de la fête de Gioventù Nazionale, le mouvement de jeunesse de son parti Fratelli d’Italia. Elle a notamment affirmé qu’il n’était pas acceptable que des élèves italiens se retrouvent en situation minoritaire dans leur propre classe. L’Italie dispose déjà d’une limite administrative de 30 % concernant les élèves non italiens dans les classes, instaurée par une circulaire ministérielle de 2010. Cette règle a toutefois été difficile à appliquer dans certaines zones, notamment en raison des réalités démographiques locales et du manque de souplesse du dispositif. Le nouveau projet annoncé par Meloni viserait donc à inscrire une limitation dans la loi. Des responsables d’établissements ont déjà souligné les difficultés pratiques que pourrait poser son application, notamment dans les quartiers où la concentration d’élèves issus de l’immigration est importante. La proposition du gouvernement italien suscite également des interrogations sur sa compatibilité avec les principes constitutionnels et sur ses modalités d’application. Des chefs d’établissement ont, de leur côté, souligné la difficulté de déplacer des élèves lorsque les familles souhaitent scolariser leurs enfants dans l’école de leur quartier. Le projet doit désormais être présenté au Conseil des ministres avant d’éventuelles étapes législatives. The post Italie : Meloni veut interdire le niqab et la burqa à l’école et limiter le nombre d’élèves étrangers appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Iran shows willingness to return to negotiating table
items.description: • Naqvi meets Pezeshkian, Momeni to ‘discuss mediation process’ • Iran ‘grateful’ to Pakistan’s political, military leadership for peace efforts • US refuses visas to some members of Iranian president’s delegation • Second Qatari LNG cargo ship ‘cleared by Iranians’ due today ISLAMABAD: Iran on Monday indicated its willingness to return to dialogue with the United States to de-escalate tensions. The flexibility on the issue was indicated by the Iranian side during a meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who is in the Iranian capital in an attempt to revive the stalled diplomatic process between Washington and Tehran. “Yes, there was progress during the meeting,” a source told Dawn . Mr Naqvi, who arrived in Tehran on Monday, was received by his Iranian counterpart Eskandar Momeni. “We had discussions on the mediation process,” Mr Naqvi said while talking to media in the presence of his Iranian counterpart. During the meeting, Mr Momeni said Iran was thankful to Pakistan’s political and military leadership for its efforts for regional peace and stability. “We are grateful to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir for their efforts for regional peace,” the Iranian minister was quoted as saying in a statement issued here by the interior ministry. The visit comes at a time when diplomatic activity has intensified to prevent another round of escalation between Iran and US, with both Qatar and Pakistan maintaining contacts with the two sides. Qatar has in recent we­­eks emerged as a key channel between Wa­­sh­ing­ton and Tehran. Its foreign ministry said on Monday that its mediation team had been exchanging ideas with both sides for nearly two weeks in an effort to bridge differences and find a suitable moment to resume negotiations. Iran relays conditions for talks Iran has conveyed through Qatar a set of conditions for reopening talks, including an end to fighting on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian assets and an end to the US naval blockade. Iranian officials said seven conditions were conveyed, although all of them were not publicly disclosed. The latest diplomatic activity follows the collapse of the 14 point Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding brokered by Pakistan on June 17. The conflict has since continued with sporadic strikes and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, while Iran has maintained control over traffic through the strategic waterway. Pakistan, meanwhile, has remained engaged in efforts to keep the diplomatic channel open. Field Marshal Asim Munir has used his contacts with the US administration while Pakistani officials have made repeated visits to Tehran. The latest visit also carries significance ahead of Mr Pezeshkian’s travel to New York for the United Nations General Assembly. The Iranian president is expected to meet Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the sidelines of the UNGA in the coming days. The meeting could provide another opportunity for the two leaders to discuss the stalled peace process. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has given mixed signals on the prospects of renewed negotiations, while Ira­nian officials have continued to combine their readiness for diplomacy with warnings of a strong response to any fresh US military action. The possibility of renewed diplomacy is also being backed by developments around the Strait of Hormuz, where Pakistan has quietly secured the passage of another Qatari liquefied natural gas shipment after negotiations with Iran. The shipment crossed the strait over the weekend and is expected to reach Pakistan’s LNG import facility by Tuesday, making it the second Qatari LNG cargo to reach Pakistan this month through an understanding with Iran. No visa from US Separately, the US refu­sed to issue visas to members of President Pezesh­kian’s delegation, including his communications team, for his trip to the UN General Assembly, Iranian state media reported. President Peze­shkian will be the highest-ranking Iranian official to enter the United States since the Middle East war began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, part of the delegation to the UN, left Iran on Sunday evening for a stopover in Qatar. Foreign ministry spok­esman Esmaeil Baqaei accused the Trump administration of “trampling on the right of access to information”, pointing to its recent move to bar three major US media outlets from the White House over objections to their coverage. “When an administration slams its doors shut — even on American journalists it happens to dislike — and bars foreign reporters, including the Iranian president’s media team, whose voices it would rather silence, it is not managing access; it is trying to hide the truth,” Baqaei said on X. Iranian airlines to be ‘shut down’ from tomorrow US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Iranian airlines will have trouble functioning globally in two days under the weight of American sanctions. On Sept 23, “all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world,” Bessent told CNBC in an interview as the war launched by the United States and Israel nears the seven-month mark. “If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he added.Two Iraqi sources told AFP on Monday that Baghdad would suspend flights by Iranian airlines following the US Treasury’s announcement. Georgia also barred Iranian carriers from its land, while Iranian airline Mahan said it suspended service to Turkiye at the re­­quest of the Turkish government. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026
